items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had also formed a quartet with four young Franch musicians, Bernard Estardy, piano, Nino Ferrer, bass, Peter Giger, drums and Charles Barrié, sax-tenor.

ctx.x: We had a very good friend, Leopold de Lima e Silva who was the son of Mistinguett, the famous Music Hall star. Leopold had inherited from his mother a very nice house with a big garden. It was called the Bungalow and was situated at the Cap d'Antibes, between Antibes and Juan-les-Pins, a 10 minute walk to the "Vieux Colombier". The house was separated in two flats, one was empty and Leopold had proposed to us to live there for a very mild rent and of course we had accepted with joy.

The day after our arrival, I had rehearsal with the band and it was terrible. We tried for two hours to rehearse "Caravan" and another number but it was must impossible. Most of those kids couldn't read, and they had no experience at all. It would have taken weeks to try to teach them to play correctly a dozen numbers. I went to see Badel and told him to look for another band. He wanted to put the blame on me because I had accepted to play with them in Paris. I wanted to put the blame on him because we had told…

Every night before my first passage, a group of young rock and rollers were playing for a half hour. It was the beginning in France of the rock and roll era. This group was called the "Chaussettes Noires" (black socks) and featuring a young singer named Eddie Mitchell.
